title: Multitenant metering drift causing billing statement variance for Dedicated/Hosted customers
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported month-to-date invoice amounts that exceeded the tokens observed in their application logs. Affected customers span Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Initial support investigation found per-hour rollups that produced higher billed token counts than the request-level accounting. This ticket tracks triage, short-term mitigation, and long-term fixes for multi-tenant metering drift that caused customer billing variance.
timeline: 2026-03-08 08:12 UTC: Customer A (Dedicated) opened escalation with account team; reported 14% higher monthly invoice vs internal logs.
2026-03-08 09:05 UTC: Support created case; assigned to on-call SRE and billing engineer.
2026-03-08 12:40 UTC: Additional reports received from Hosted customers in EU region showing smaller deltas (~2-6%).
2026-03-09 03:25 UTC: Pager duty incident declared (INC-2026-03-MTR). Engineering on-call joined bridge.
2026-03-09 10:15 UTC: Temporary mitigation - throttled background aggregation job and paused hourly rollup job for affected clusters.
2026-03-10 16:00 UTC: Root cause hypothesis formed: aggregation worker double-counting on fallback routing + rollup window overlap across DST boundary in EU causing tenant attribution leakage.
2026-03-11 09:30 UTC: Hotfix deployed to tag aggregation messages with billing_account_id and deployment_id; immediately reduced new variance reports.
2026-03-12 14:00 UTC: Reconciliation batch started to recompute last 30 days for top 10 affected customers; credits pre-approved for identified overcharges.

reproduction_steps: 1) Run mixed routing workload with primary model on Dedicated pool A and fallback to Hosted variant B under high concurrency (>500 qps).
2) Enable continuous batching and prefix KV cache while toggling fallback policy that routes individual requests between pools.
3) Start hourly rollup aggregation worker that groups metrics by hour using server-local clock (no tenant tag) and observe token counts aggregated to worker instance's local tenant mapping.
4) Simulate DST clock change / clock skew between aggregation nodes and observe doubled attribution for requests crossing batching boundaries.
root_cause: Two interacting problems: 1) The aggregation worker used a worker-local mapping to attribute token counts to tenants and did not carry a stable billing_account_id tag from the serving layer; when a request was routed to a fallback model (hosted or alternate deployment), the aggregator sometimes saw two events for the same logical request — once with the serving node's tenant mapping and once from the fallback path. 2) Hourly rollup windows were computed using local node clock windows; clock skew/DST transitions caused partial windows to be processed twice and occasionally reassigned across worker shard boundaries, producing small-but-cumulative overcounts across tenants. Additionally, small FX rounding rules in the billing pipeline magnified token deltas into visible invoice differences for multi-currency accounts.
mitigation: Short-term: 1) Paused the hourly rollup worker cluster to stop further accrual of misattributed tokens. 2) Deployed hotfix (billing-tag-propagation v0.1) to serving runtime that attaches stable billing_account_id and deployment_id to every metering event before any fallback routing. 3) Issued proactive credits to top affected customers pending reconciliation and communicated timeline. 4) Added temporary alert thresholds on per-tenant token vs observed request deltas (above 5% over rolling 7-day window).
long_term_fix: 1) Move token accounting to request-bound attribution in the serving runtime so every token increment is tagged atomically with billing_account_id and model_variant_id and emitted once. 2) Rework aggregation service to use strictly monotonic, cluster-wide time windows (bucketed by UTC epoch seconds) and validate idempotence on replays. 3) Add E2E convergence tests that simulate fallback routing under load. 4) Update billing pipeline FX handling to minimize rounding amplification and add automated reconciliation runs with ledger checkpoints. 5) Expand canary and observability: per-tenant token parity dashboards, anomaly detection, and a reconciliation playbook with automated credit generation.
actions_taken: Hotfix deployed: billing-tag-propagation v0.1 -> reduced incoming misattribution by >90% for new traffic.
Aggregation rollup paused for 4 affected clusters at 2026-03-09 10:30 UTC.
Recompute job started for last 30 days for top 25 customers; interim credits offered to top 10 (approx $48k total across customers).
Customer communications: initial notice sent 2026-03-09 18:00 UTC; follow-up email with technical summary and timeline sent 2026-03-12 20:00 UTC.
Incident bridge notes and recording uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/metering-INC-2026-03
playbook_updates: Add a step to the metering incident playbook to verify billing_account_id propagation end-to-end before enabling any fallback routing for multi-tenant clusters.
Document reconciliation thresholds and automated credit approval rules for invoices with >3% discrepancy.
Add scheduled monthly ledger checkpoint job and reconciler tests.

outage_window: No customer-facing outage. Internal reconciliation lag and invoice variance window: 2026-02-25 to 2026-03-08.

Finish full recompute for all customers and finalize credits by 2026-03-20.
